subject: Architecture
title: Fire Safety: Lessons Written in Tragedy
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Fire Safety: Lessons Written in Tragedy.

hook.text: Skyscraper fire codes exist because people died. Every rule has a story behind it.

buildup.text: Stairwells must be pressurized, fire doors self-closing, and sprinklers on every floor.

discovery.text: Fireproofing coats every steel beam — steel loses half its strength at 1,100°F, well within fire range.

twist.text: The Grenfell Tower fire in 2017 revealed that cladding materials could spread flames up a building's exterior.

climax.text: After Grenfell, countries worldwide banned combustible cladding and rechecked thousands of buildings.

punchline.text: Every fire code is a memorial. The rules exist because something failed.

quiz.question: At what temperature does steel lose half its structural strength?
